subject: QBR prep: inference capacity signalbook & unit cost scenarios
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, miriam@atlas-ai.com, procurement@atlas-ai.com
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: inference capacity signalbook & unit cost scenarios

Team — attaching a lightweight signalbook for the QBR. High level ask: we need a 2-slide summary (1) current capacity run-rate + headroom, (2) three realistic cost scenarios with proposed mitigations and a short recommendation. Attachments: QBR_inference_signalbook_v1.pptx and utilization_run_rates_may2027.csv.

Quick summary of the numbers at the moment (baseline = hosted + dedicated blended):
- Current monthly GPU spend (net) = $1.92M.
- Active GPU hours this month = 62.4k hrs; fleet-weighted utilization = 58% (goal 70–75%).
- Short-tail traffic: P95 latency on gen routes = 245ms; batching at our current settings reduces token cost by ~18% but increases P95 by ~20ms on average.
- KV/prefix caching trial is showing ~12% token reduction on steady-state routes (chat embeddings-heavy customers).

Scenarios to include for the QBR:
A) Base (no action): current spend, utilization holds — runway comfortable for 2.8 months.
B) End-of-quarter demand spike (+30% sustained for 10 days): risk of hitting request throttles on hosted tier; projected extra spend +$360k unless we shift routing.
C) Aggressive optimization (batching + cache tunings + quantize N4->N3 for cold stack): expected unit cost down 22% but 95th latency increases on some routes — model quality risk needs a note.

Operational asks from me:
- Lauren: can you split the spend into hosted vs dedicated and call out any committed-reserve opportunities that would reduce blended per-token? (slide 1)
- Vivek: please include the scheduling/commitment windows and whether we can gate a small 10% buffer for end-of-quarter promotions (I flagged a potential partner listing that may spike Q4 bookings).
- Olga: please take the numbers and produce a 1-page risk table with mitigations and rollback triggers (canary thresholds, fallback models, region routing).

External note to Atlas: Miriam / procurement — we included your requested headroom scenarios and a conservative planned burst profile (see slide 4 in deck). If you can confirm the expected growth spike next month, we can propose a short-term reserved pool to avoid throttling.

Thanks — Soojin

Soojin Lee
Director, Product (Inference)
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, miriam@atlas-ai.com, procurement@atlas-ai.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: inference capacity signalbook & unit cost scenarios

Thanks Soojin — good framing. A few clarifying asks before I split the slides: 
1) Hosted vs Dedicated split — is the $1.92M number gross or net of marketplace credits/partner discounts? I want net to be transparent.
2) Can you paste the fleet utilization by model family (Llama-variants vs. Redwood-verified quant-variants)? That will determine which units are the best candidates for batch-heavy tuning.
3) Please call out quantization quality risk explicitly if we surface the aggressive optimization scenario (we need a simple evaluation metric or two to say "no meaningful regression" for the execs).

I will take slide 1 and create a 1/2 slide that shows spend split and a small chart with utilization by model family. Vivek — if you have the commit/contract windows handy, paste here and I'll annotate with how much cost reduction we can get at 6/12/24 month terms.

-Lauren

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, miriam@atlas-ai.com, procurement@atlas-ai.com
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: inference capacity signalbook & unit cost scenarios

Adding context from infra ops: 
- The $1.92M is net of standard marketplace discounts but does not reflect the two pilot reserved pools (one for internal RD, one for a key partner) — those are accounted for elsewhere and would reduce external billable spend by ~6% if we convert pilots to committed in June.
- We have a scheduled marketing promotion window 06/28–07/02 that historically produces a short burst (~30% peak increase for 4–7 days). If Atlas confirms a marketing push for early June we should pre-provision or shift routing to dedicated tiers for those routes.
- Recommendation: provision a 10% committed buffer for the month of June to avoid emergency hot-swap that costs more in spot/premium. That buffer costs ~+$48k/month but prevents potential $360k emergency spend in the spike scenario.

Operational note: autoscaler tuning request — reduce max batch latency threshold on gen-critical routes to 60ms (today 90ms) as an intermediate step before more aggressive batching. That preserves P95 for latency-sensitive customers while still capturing batching benefits for background tasks.

-Vivek

Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep: inference capacity signalbook & unit cost scenarios

Thanks everyone — I pulled the numbers into the attached CSV and added a compact risk table to slide 2 of the deck. The short version:
- Mitigations we can execute this week: enable region-aware routing for bursty Atlas traffic; raise canary rollback sensitivity to 10% quality delta; enable a short-lived 10% reserved buffer (Vivek's ask).
- Key rollback/cutover triggers: sustained P95 > 320ms, error rate +0.6pp vs baseline, or quant eval metric drop > 2% on the held-out prompt set.

Miriam — one action for you: can you confirm whether Atlas will run the mid-June awareness campaign? If yes, we will recommend a short-term committed reserve and route their traffic to dedicated capacity for the weekend window. Procurement — I'll include a small negotiated concession (1 week grace on unused committed buffer) to keep cost predictable.

Link to updated deck: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qZq-Infra-QBR-Prep (slide 2 = risk matrix; slide 4 = headroom scenarios).
